partners.mechanism_chain: MID1 (HGNC:7467) —DISRUPTS→ Microtubule organization and intracellular transport (GO:0007017); Microtubule organization and intracellular transport (GO:0007017) —LEADS_TO→ Epithelial-mesenchymal transition (GO:0001837); Epithelial-mesenchymal transition (GO:0001837) —DISRUPTS→ Craniofacial development (GO:0001657); IRF6 (HGNC:5956) —DISRUPTS→ Epithelial-mesenchymal transition (GO:0001837); Epithelial-mesenchymal transition (GO:0001837) —LEADS_TO→ Craniofacial development (GO:0001657); Craniofacial development (GO:0001657) —LEADS_TO→ Opitz G/BBB syndrome (MONDO:0010222); Craniofacial development (GO:0001657) —LEADS_TO→ van der Woude syndrome 1 (MONDO:0007333). #### 1. van der Woude syndrome 1  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.450)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-877300)

**Proposed mechanism:** MID1 (HGNC:7467) —DISRUPTS→ Microtubule organization and intracellular transport (GO:0007017); Microtubule organization and intracellular transport (GO:0007017) —LEADS_TO→ Epithelial-mesenchymal transition (GO:0001837); Epithelial-mesenchymal transition (GO:0001837) —DISRUPTS→ Craniofacial development (GO:0001657); IRF6 (HGNC:5956) —DISRUPTS→ Epithelial-mesenchymal transition (GO:0001837); Epithelial-mesenchymal transition (GO:0001837) —LEADS_TO→ Craniofacial development (GO:0001657); Craniofacial development (GO:0001657) —LEADS_TO→ Opitz G/BBB syndrome (MONDO:0010222); Craniofacial development (GO:0001657) —LEADS_TO→ van der Woude syndrome 1 (MONDO:0007333). Loss of function in MID1 disrupts microtubule organization and intracellular transport, which indirectly affects epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) required for craniofacial development. Similarly, loss of function in IRF6 directly impairs EMT, a critical process for craniofacial development. Both pathways converge on the disruption of normal EMT processes, leading to distinct but related craniofacial phenotypes.

**How to falsify it:** If genetic studies reveal that mutations in MID1 or IRF6 do not affect epithelial-mesenchymal transition or craniofacial development in model systems, or if distinct molecular pathways unrelated to EMT are identified as the primary drivers for each disease. _(variant: A common pathogenic variant (AF > 0.001) in MID1 or IRF6 associated with these diseases.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared downstream impact on epithelial-mesenchymal transition in craniofacial development could reveal common therapeutic targets for managing the craniofacial anomalies seen in both X-linked Opitz G/BBB syndrome and van der Woude syndrome 1.
